topic: The Fourier Transform: Decoding the DNA of Signals

sections.title: The Big Idea: The Smoothie Metaphor
lecture_lines: Imagine a complex signal is like a fruit smoothie.
It is a mixture of different ingredients blended together.
The Fourier Transform acts like a magical filter.
It pulls out individual ingredients, like strawberries or bananas.
We move from time-based signals to distinct frequencies.
animations: Show a complex, jagged red wave #FF5555 titled 'Sound Smoothie'.
A white icon #FFFFFF representing a chef appears next to the wave.
A blue filter #00AAFF moves through the red wave, separating it.
The red wave splits into three colored sine waves: #FF0000, #00FF00, #5555FF.
Labels 'Time Domain' #AAAAAA and 'Frequency Domain' #FFFFFF appear for contrast.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Building Blocks
lecture_lines: Basic sine waves are our fundamental building blocks.
They vary by their frequency and their amplitude.
Any complex wave is just a sum of these.
animations: Display three tuning forks colored #FF0000, #00FF00, and #5555FF.
Show each fork vibrating with its own colored sine wave.
Merge the three waves into one complex purple wave #A020F0.

sections.title: The Winding Machine (Visual Intuition)
lecture_lines: Let's wrap our signal around a circular pole.
At most frequencies, the result is a chaotic scribble.
But at the magic frequency, a pattern emerges.
The center of mass shifts far from the origin.
This shift marks a hidden component of the signal.
animations: A white circle #FFFFFF appears with a rotating vector inside.
Wrap a signal around the circle creating a gray scribble #888888.
Highlight a yellow dot #FFFF00 at the circle's center (Center of Mass).
Adjust winding frequency so the scribble shifts to the right.
The yellow dot #FFFF00 moves away, creating a white spike #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Connecting to the Math
lecture_lines: The formula captures this winding process mathematically.
Euler's formula rotates our signal around the complex plane.
Integrating over time finds the average center of mass.
Peaks appear on the spectrum at component frequencies.
This transforms time data into a frequency map.
animations: Display the formula X(f) = integral x(t) exp(-i 2pi ft) dt in #FFFFFF.
Highlight x(t) in red #FF0000 and label it 'Signal'.
Highlight exp(-i 2pi ft) in blue #00AAFF and label it 'Winder'.
Highlight the integral and dt in green #00FF00 (label: 'Center of Mass').
Show a sharp yellow peak #FFFF00 on a frequency graph.

sections.title: Application: Noise Cancellation
lecture_lines: We can use this map to edit reality.
Identify and delete spikes representing unwanted noise.
Transform back to hear only the clear voice.
animations: Show a green voice wave #00FF00 with red noise #FF0000 fuzz.
In the frequency domain, identify and delete the noise spike.
Reconstruct the signal to show only the clean green wave.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
lecture_lines: The Fourier Transform reveals the hidden DNA of signals.
It splits complex waves into their pure components.
A powerful lens for understanding our physical universe.
animations: A complex white wave #FFFFFF hits a blue prism #00AAFF.
The prism outputs a rainbow of distinct frequency lines.
Text 'Decoding the DNA of Signals' #FFFFFF appears and expands.
